headings.title: Administration, enforcement, and pesticide use regulations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and source notes (L. 1974 S.B. 431 § 4, as amended through A.L. 2021 H.B. 476 merged with S.B. 26; effective 1-01-25, see § 281.102). Assigns administration and enforcement of §§ 281.010 to 281.115 to the director, authorizes chapter 536 regulations after at least thirty days' notice and a public hearing covering pesticide use conditions, area/time restrictions, research consideration, and optional adjoining-landowner notice regulations.

headings.title: Restricted use pesticide list and additional restrictions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and source notes (effective 1-01-25, see § 281.102). Adopts the federal restricted use pesticide list in Missouri, requires annual publication available upon request, and subjects pesticides posing unreasonable adverse environmental effects to certified-applicator supervision and additional director restrictions on possession and use.

headings.title: Public hearing and mail notice for regulations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and source notes (effective 1-01-25, see § 281.102). Prohibits adopting, amending, or repealing regulations under §§ 281.010 to 281.115 without a public hearing held after at least thirty days' prior regular-mail notice to persons registered with the director for hearing notices.

headings.title: Hearing participation, written comments, and action notices
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and source notes (effective 1-01-25, see § 281.102). Covers opportunity to be heard upon written request received at least twenty-four hours before the hearing, seven-day post-hearing written statements of views, optional written solicitation by the director, and written notice of the director's action to participants or requesters.

headings.title: Rulemaking compliance with section 536.024
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and source notes (effective 1-01-25, see § 281.102). Conditions effectiveness of any rule or portion of a rule promulgated under chapter 281 on promulgation pursuant to § 536.024.

Authorizes the director by regulation to classify §§ 281.010 to 281.115 licenses (including commercial, noncommercial, private, provisional private, public operator, pesticide technician, and noncertified RUP applicator) and specify separate ground, aerial, or manual methods.

headings.title: Certification categories, testing, and single-fee rule
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and source notes (effective 1-01-25, see § 281.102). Authorizes certification categories under each license classification with separate testing procedures, prohibits additional fees for certification in multiple categories under one applied-for license, and permits limited-pesticide certification categories with tailored testing.

headings.title: Fees for identification documents
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and source notes (effective 1-01-25, see § 281.102). Authorizes the director by regulation to establish fees for identification documents.

headings.title: Commercial applicator license, fee, supervision, and employment notice
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and source notes (L. 1974 S.B. 431 § 6, as amended through A.L. 2021 H.B. 476 merged with S.B. 26; effective 1-01-25, see § 281.102). Requires a certified commercial applicator license and category certification for commercial pesticide business on lands of another, sets a $65 annual fee, restricts authorizing general use or minimum risk pesticide work to pesticide technicians/trainees or directly supervised individuals with applicator liability, and mandates ten-day written notice of technician or trainee employment.

headings.title: Supervising noncertified RUP applicators and applicator liability
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and source notes (effective 1-01-25, see § 281.102). Prohibits a certified commercial applicator from knowingly authorizing, directing, or instructing an individual to determine need for or use restricted use pesticides on another's land unless licensed as a noncertified RUP applicator under direct supervision, with supervising applicator liability.

headings.title: Commercial applicator license application form and contents
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and source notes (effective 1-01-25, see § 281.102). Requires commercial applicator license applications to be submitted on a designated department form containing information prescribed by regulation.

headings.title: Certification examination requirements for commercial applicators
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and source notes (effective 1-01-25, see § 281.102). Bars issuance of a certified commercial applicator license until the applicant passes a director-provided examination demonstrating competence and knowledge of proper pesticide use and certification standards.

headings.title: License renewal by recertification training or reexamination
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and source notes (effective 1-01-25, see § 281.102). Authorizes the director to renew a certified commercial applicator license upon successful completion of approved recertification training or reexamination.

headings.title: License issuance, term, limitations, and written denial
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and source notes (effective 1-01-25, see § 281.102). Directs issuance of a one-year certified commercial applicator license upon qualification and § 281.065 bond/insurance compliance (or earlier expiration matching financial responsibility), allows scope/area/equipment limitations, and requires written reasons if not issued as applied for.

headings.title: Three-year pesticide application recordkeeping and copies
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 and source notes (effective 1-01-25, see § 281.102). Requires certified commercial applicators or their employers to keep pesticide application records (including directly supervised technicians, trainees, and noncertified RUP applicators) for three years and furnish copies upon written request by the director.

headings.title: Temporary operations during sole commercial applicator absence
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 8 and source notes (effective 1-01-25, see § 281.102). Allows a business deprived of its sole certified commercial applicator by death, illness, incapacity, or unavoidable absence to continue operations for a director-approved period up to sixty days without using restricted use pesticides, with immediate notice to the director.

headings.title: Prominent display of commercial applicator license
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 9 and source notes (effective 1-01-25, see § 281.102). Requires every certified commercial applicator to display the license prominently at the operating site, location, or office printed on the license.

headings.title: Address change notice and no-fee revised license
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 10 and source notes (effective 1-01-25, see § 281.102). Requires immediate notice to the director upon changing operating address and directs immediate issuance of a revised license without fee retaining the original expiration date.

headings.title: Prominent display of noncommercial applicator license
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 10 and source notes (effective 1-01-25, see § 281.102). Requires every certified noncommercial applicator to display the license prominently at the operating site, location, or office printed on the license.

headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 11 and source notes (effective 1-01-25, see § 281.102). Requires immediate address-change notification to the director and immediate issuance of a revised license without fee keeping the original expiration date.

headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and source notes (effective 1-01-25, see § 281.102). Authorizes renewing a pesticide technician license upon completing an additional approved training program to the director's satisfaction as prescribed by regulation.

headings.title: Assessment of condemnation costs against intervening claimants
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note (L. 1955 p. 26 § 9, as amended through A.L. 1982 H.B. 1514). Awards court costs, fees, storage, and other proper expenses against any intervening claimant when a condemnation decree is entered.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 281.300:14966, all four subsections including subdivisions (1)–(3) of subsection 1, and history note (L. 1955 p. 26 § 9, A.L. 1978 H.B. 1634, A.L. 1982 H.B. 1514 §§ 263.350, 263.360); verified sourceUrl, sourceSha256, textSha256, and every subsection bodySha256. Verified retention of verbatim source spelling 'adultered' in subsection 1(1), destruction/sale disposal and relabeling bond in subsection 2, stop sale/use/removal orders covering pesticides or devices with release and 30-day permissive/mandatory condemnation triggers in subsection 3, and intervening-claimant cost awards in subsection 4. Revised subsection 3 to include the 30-day condemnation proceedings trigger; retained subsections 1, 2, and 4.

headings.title: Infraction penalty for section 281.240 subsection 1(1) violations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1955 p. 26 § 8, A.L. 1982 H.B. 1514). Makes violations of § 281.240(1)(1) an infraction punishable upon conviction by a fine up to $1,000.

headings.title: Other violation penalties, post-warning misdemeanors, and registration termination
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note (L. 1955 p. 26 § 8, A.L. 1982 H.B. 1514). Makes other §§ 281.210 to 281.310 violations (excluding § 281.240(1)(1) and subsection 3) infractions fined up to $500 first offense and $1,000 subsequent (with a five-year reset to first offense), elevates post-warning registrant violations to a class A misdemeanor with automatic registration termination (retaining verbatim source phrasing omitting 'and' before 'such registrant violates'), and requires full compliance before reregistration.

headings.title: Prohibited formula or trade-secret disclosure and misdemeanor penalty
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note (L. 1955 p. 26 § 8, A.L. 1982 H.B. 1514). Prohibits knowingly or recklessly using or revealing § 281.260 formula information or submitter-designated trade secrets or confidential information without prior written consent, punishable as a class A misdemeanor.

headings.title: Limitation to federal labeling and packaging requirements
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note (L. 1955 p. 26 § 8, A.L. 1982 H.B. 1514). States that §§ 281.210 to 281.310 shall not impose or 'continue to effect' (retaining verbatim source wording) labeling or packaging requirements in addition to or different from federal regulations.
